scope: Eight researched islands, 42 NPS-published designated site coordinates on five islands. NPS historical planning references, not surveyed present-day navigation waypoints; no live availability or trail linework generated.

coordinatePolicy.sand: omit all Sand coordinates because NPS says they are being corrected
coordinatePolicy.devils: omit coordinate because duplicated Cat entry and marina/campsite closure
coordinatePolicy.group: letter-numbered site identifier follows NPS coordinate table
coordinatePolicy.accessible: Stockton 1 and groups A/B have explicitly documented boardwalk access; Sand 3 and C likewise documented but coordinates withheld

islands.name: Stockton Island
islands.lede: From the quiet sand of Julian Bay to an old brownstone quarry, Stockton asks you to choose which shoreline you want to meet.
islands.note: Three distinct public dock approaches in the NPS list. The Presque Isle–Quarry Bay trail connection has had a bridge washout; verify trail conditions before committing.
trails: From Presque Isle ranger station to Julian Bay.
Woodland path between the Presque Isle dock and Julian Bay.
Bog and beach; lagoon outlet may require wading.
From Presque Isle toward Quarry Bay; meadow route can be indistinct.
From Quarry Bay toward the old brownstone quarry.
Unmaintained route through island interior; difficult route finding.

islands.name: Oak Island
islands.lede: This is the island of long trails: ancient beach ridges, sugar maples and overlooks high above Lake Superior.
islands.note: The NPS overlook is about 3.5 miles from the dock, not 1.8 miles from the dock. The published operator schedule was for overnight service; a same-day return must be arranged separately.
trails: Horseshoe from the public dock through the central uplands.
Branch off the loop, reaching campsite 4 about 2.8 miles from dock.
Spur from inland junction; overlook about 3.5 miles from dock.
Ravine route to campsite 6, about 4 miles from dock.
Beach and sites 1/A. Stay on established trails and bare beach.

islands.name: Sand Island
islands.lede: Walk from East Bay toward a lighthouse above the lake, or take the old roadbed into the island's cabin history.
islands.note: NPS is updating Sand Island campsite coordinates. Their previously published latitude/longitude entries are deliberately NOT plotted here. Refer to its official campsite map, posted signs and current ranger guidance.
trails: From East Bay dock north to the lighthouse; boardwalk can be slippery.
Old roadbed south past sites 2, A and B. No maintained path to Lighthouse Bay sites 4/5.
islands.withheldReason: NPS says Sand Island campsite coordinates are in the process of being corrected. No campsite pin is safe to treat as a location reference.

islands.name: Raspberry Island
islands.lede: A lighthouse above two shores and a walk through old forest. This is a landing-and-return day, not an island camping night.
islands.note: No designated campsites and no primitive camping. A published lighthouse cruise does not guarantee a landing on a given trip.
trails: From the lighthouse grounds to a west-bay viewpoint.
Old-growth forest to the southeast beach.
islands.withheldReason: There are no designated campsites on Raspberry Island. Nothing to plot.

islands.name: Michigan Island
islands.lede: Behind the light station, a trail leads toward a sandspit, then along the uncertain edge of a lagoon.
islands.note: The lagoon trail seems to stop at a bog before continuing. A sightseeing lighthouse tour may not land; confirm the actual itinerary.
trails: From the light station behind the vault toilet toward sandspit and campsite.
Bog crossing may make the route appear to end.

islands.name: Rocky Island
islands.lede: A compact network begins at the east dock, where northern campsite paths and a southern shoreline trail split.
islands.note: North Trail goes by sites 4, 5 and A. Respect private lands past Group Site A. Do not assume scheduled passenger service.
trails: Boardwalk and stairs lead to a woodland path crossing the island.
From the dock bulletin board toward the south shoreline.
Past campsites 4, 5 and A toward the island's northern shore.

islands.name: Basswood Island
islands.lede: Follow the longer loop through an abandoned farm landscape and old brownstone quarry, with a campsite path branching from the dock clearing.
islands.note: The 5.5-mile loop is not a measure of how far your campsite is from a boat landing. NPS says sites A, 5 and 6 are on the short branch from the dock-area trail intersection.
trails: NPS route through McCloud-Brigham farm landscape and brownstone quarry.

islands.name: Devils Island
islands.lede: The NPS map tells the history of a light station and its paths, but it is not an invitation to land at the closed south marina.
islands.note: South dock/marina and campsites are closed in the reviewed 2026 NPS construction information. The NPS campsite table repeats an anomalous Cat Island coordinate for Devils; do not plot it or interpret it as a valid campsite location.
trails: Historical link to a natural rock landing; not a recommended landing approach.
Historical light-station path; not a current access plan.
Historic trail from the light station to the closed south harbor.
islands.withheldReason: Closed marina and campsite access. The published Devils campsite coordinate is anomalous and excluded.
